post_title: gpu  is not used in simulation only cpu
post_details: HI, maybe I miss something , I am starting with some basic stuff ,just creating a basic t-shirt and I try to simulate with GPU, but I check it and CPU is used instead of cpu. I have a RTX 3060 and AMD 7700x. some hints? thanks

comments.comment_body: You are likely experiencing this issue because Marvelous Designer does not support AMD graphics cards for GPU simulation: see the manual link here https://marvelousdesigner.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/9848688288665-System-Requirements LUCKILY you want to be working in CPU for your workflow anyway. GPU simulation is inaccurate and has inaccurate simulation. Here is the workflow order from our discord channel and invite here https://discord.gg/HAh568h Workflows for simulation in ORDER: 1. GPU - use at start if necessary. Best for large amounts of fabric. Not good for accuracy, not meant for anything other than settling large amounts of cloth into the scene at FIRST. WILL have collision issues, not accurate cloth sim. PLEASE DO NOT KEEP WORKING IN GPU you will encounter inaccuracies and "bugs" 2. CPU - Recommended use: Majority of workflow. What you want to work in until the end for final simulation, can also be the final simulation stage depending on workflow. Accurate cloth simulation, most recommended simulation option. Used in all official tutorials unless stated otherwise 3. Accurate Fabric -Use at end if necessary: slowest, most accurate for real life simulation, used to remove skin offset &amp additional collision thickness (may not in V12)

post_title: Import avatar(.fbx) and apply texture

comments.comment_body: Thank you for contacting us, First of all, you need to import your garment and character separately. You need to import your character mesh as "Avatar" for "Object Type" during import. And for garment file, you would need to use .OBJ file format and chose "Garment" for "Object Type". If you import your garment using OBJ, you can simulate but the parameters you can adjust is limited. You would not able to assign fabric to it. However, Marvelous Designer does not have a render engine build inside. The textures for the fabrics in Marvelous designer are also built with diffuse and normal maps. You are still able to use it in the render engine you are using. You can also check the "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map" option during your .OBJ import if you have proper UV for your mesh. By checking this, Marvelous Designer will create pattern pieces base on your UV shell. Patterns will show up in the 2D window, and you will be able to use all of the functions in Marvelous Designer. This might be best method for you. For tutorial on "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map", please watch this tutorial here [LINK] I would strongly recommend you to watch our Quick Start tutorials to learn the basics in using Marvelous Designer, you can find these tutorials here [LINK] I also recommend you to join our discord channel, you would get faster respond from you peer here. [Discord Invite Link] Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

comments.comment_body: This is likely due to everything being imported into Marvelous Designer at FAR too small of a scale (You can tell by how large the grid is to the avatar, you can also compare its height to the default avatars for example). Watch the ENTIRETY of this YouTube video from our channel covering the issues when you import your avatar/ assets TOO SMALL for the scene like you have above. Hi Lai Edgar, Thank you for contacting us, The reason why this is happening is because your character scale is too small. The default unit in Marvelous designer is millimeter, and your character is currently only around 20 millimeters tall. When import your character, you can set the import scale, please make sure your character is at a similar size as the avatars in the Marvelous Designer library. You are able to change the subdivision of the mesh using the particle distance setting in the property editor. a lower particle distance will make the mesh denser. randomized triangle will produced the most realist cloth quality in simulation, since the mesh can only be bend along the edges of the geometry. So when you import your .OBJ and checked "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map", Marvelous designer will recreate your garment by tracing your mesh UV. If you want to simulate with your original remeshed geometry, please uncheck "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map" but still import it as a garment. Please note that, by unchecking "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map", you are able to simulate, but the amount of parameters and properties you are able to adjust is limited. Please watch our Quick start Tutorials for more information on the above subjects [Link] Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

post_title: Auto-fitting works but pattern curvature is not maintained
post_details: Hello, I am following all of the steps for auto fitting. 1. Create avatar fitting suit and garment fitting suit, simulate. 2. Add garment to avatar, change particle distance to 20. 3. Simulate. 4. Garment fits on avatar *** PROBLEM : the garment looks like it fits, however in the 2d pattern window you can tell how messed up it is. The curvature and the lines completely change and throw off the look of the garment. Please let me know what I am doing wrong. I added screenshots of pattern before and after auto fitting so you can see the difference in the lines. Also added screenshots of avatar and garment fitting suit! Thank you!

comments.comment_body: The result you are seeing is what you should be expecting from the tool. When you are using the Auto Fitting Tools the pattern will never be exact to what the original was, due to the nature of how the concept of resizing works and how different the avatar is from the original. (think morph target) Even in the real world concept of "grading": changes and warp to patterns will occur and need to be accounted for in each "size". Imagine trying to scale a 3 piece suit from a XXL too a small, or visa versa, or even making a custom suit: that pattern/garment will need clean up to make it fit as intended on each body type. In terms of Fit Suit Best practices: make sure its as clean and accurate as you can make it, any errors will be applied as "correct" when you change the size. AKA: If your " 'if than' rule has an error, your results will appear incorrect" Pattern best practices: Remove all superfluous segment points and work with curve points to make your work more efficient and the changes easier to adjust. IF you don't know what is the difference between those two: please watch any of our beginner patterning tutorials. &lt&lt&ltLINK TLDR: That is what you should expect, Auto fitting will get you MOST of the way to the answer you want but it will ALWAYS require clean up.

comments.comment_body: Oh man, I have been having this exact same issue with for 2 years, with MD10 not working for me (MD9 does). And I've run the OpenGL Viewer like you and got the same answers.... I have RTX 3090's as well (two of) and I have been pulling my hair out for 2 whole years, with no solution from Support unfortunately that worked for me. A beverage of your choice to anyone who manages to figure out this problem! (can't wait to solve this!).

I finally figured it out! I don't know if this will help many others with this issue but at least in my case, I had an system-wide environmental variable set: QT_OPENGL=angle deleting this environmental variable or changing it to QT_OPENGL=desktop finally fixed the issue.
Brilliant news Allen, well done! Where/how do you change that variable, I'm struggling where to find it :)

Found it!!!! You sir are a genius! How the hell did you fathom that one out? I've been contacting MD support for a LONG time and in the end, both they and I gave up.... and here, nearly two years later, your good self has done it!!! Thank you soooo much :)

I'm so glad this was able to help someone else struggling with this issue! There is little or no info to be had when googling the error I too was pulling my hair out for a long time. To answer your question: I knew Marvelous Designer is written with QT. QT is an open-source universal application development platform used by a great many Windows and Mac applications. Trying to find out where the error is being triggered from, I started the MD app inside a debugger and saw it gets it's cue weather or not to show the OpenGL error dialog from a QOpenGL class. I did some research on OpenGL errors in QT and it led me to this github post (https://github.com/CauldronDevelopmentLLC/CAMotics/issues/301) and found the info about the QT_OPENGL environmental variable being set incorrectly. I checked it on my machine and low and behold it was set incorrectly. It must have been set by another app or I put it in there at some point as I dabble in QT development from time to time.

Woah, I have been waiting absolutely years for someone to figure it out. I would really appreciate it if you could help me fix this! I don't have as much knowledge as you but I have done my best to try and follow your steps. So I have installed QT creator (is this correct?) but I don't know how or what to open so I can get to the point of changing the variable to desktop. Would it be possible to get your great brain on this!? G
13709610200985 Windows + R Type "sysdm.cpl" - press Enter. Go to the Advanced Tab and Select "Environment Variables". From there, you can find the QT_OpenGL=Angle and change that to =Desktop.

Thank you for your response and your help. I still have one more point that I don't understand, I've already watched a lot of videos from your platform. But unfortunately, I still can't figure out how to get such folds.. I just made them, but they are very sharp... And in my version, they are sharp at the beginning and then smoothed out... I've changed almost all kinds of fabric... Lowered the particle distance. But alas, it doesn't help much, maybe I was close but I missed something... ??? Here's what happened And these are all my refs

The fold can be created using the internal lines. To get the kind of fold from your reference where it is folded at the top and loose at the bottom, The internal lines should not run all the way down to the end. You would also need to mess with the settings of the internal lines Fold Angle: The value of fold angle is in between 0 to 360, 180 represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360. Fold Strength: The intensity of the fold is able to be set by adjusting the value of Fold Strength. The higher the value, the closer the fold is to the set angle. When a jacket and its lining are sewn together, the sewn area inflates due to the default sewing angle and intensity values. In this case, sets the Fold Strength to 0 to flatten the sewn boundaries. Turning off Fold rendering will smooth out the normal of the geometry and the line will look smooth instead of a sharp fold. I would also recommend you to join our discord channel, where you can get faster respond to your questions : [Discord Invite Link] Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

post_title: Smooth Avatar Saving and Performance
post_details: Hi everyone. This is more a heads up than a question. Yet there might be a question in there somewhere. For the longest time I had the issue of projects becoming less performant over time. I just found out why and would like to share. Its fairly simple, and many might already know. I didnt, and thats kind of the problem.. Every time I checked the box for smooth avatar and saved the scene, the smoothing level gets saved as well. So when I reload the scene, the avatar is already smoothed. The issue lies within the check box, as it does not represent the actual smoothing state anymore. While the avatar is already smoothed upon re-loading the scene, the checkbox is unchecked, so i assumed the avatar wasnt smoothed. I feel kinda stupid that I never thought about this before, yet here I am. This might be covered in the manual, but who reads a manual really.. To make this post a worthy contender for the Help Center, i'd like to ask if this could get adressed, as there might be others out there wondering why performance becomes slower over time, yet everyone always talks about hardware, cpu and simmulation settings. Maybe a small hint next to the checkbox would help, or better yet, save the state of the checkbox with the scene so it becomes less confusing. If this however didnt happen to anyone but me, i apologize for my ignorance.

comments.comment_body: Hi Philipp, We apologize for the inconvenience. This is a bug and I have created a bug report on this issue. We will address this in the future patch updates. However, the smooth avatar function will subdivide the avatar. It is set to uncheck by default. You would only use it if your character mesh is not dense enough for simulation. For example, if your character is low poly and the garment intersect with the avatar because of it, you would need to subdivide the mesh. If it works well enough you wouldn't need to smooth your avatar when it is first imported. Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team
